rule: decision 47: a mapping the blind verifier did not confirm is held — never shown, never a diagnosis, never S5 evidence — until a human keeps or drops it

items.stem: A die is thrown, so the sample space is $S=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. Write the event $A$ = the event of getting an even number: tap on the number line every outcome in $A$.
items.construction: Points mode, range [-6,6]. Tap 2, 4 and 6 — all within range, whole numbers, 3 targets (≤4). Reachable.
items.predicate_meaning: Right sizes, wrong signs — a value marked as its negative, as when (x − a) = 0 is read as x = −a
items.hint: Check each marked outcome against the condition of the event.
items.why: Fires only if student marks negatives like -2,-4,-6. Nobody holding a misconception about even numbers in a die's sample space would tap negatives, and the predicate description (x−a=0 read as x=−a) is irrelevant here; the hint is generic and does not address a sign issue. The sample space has only positive outcomes, so this is a stray mis-tap rather than a sign misconception.

items.stem: A die is thrown, so the sample space is $S=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. Write the event $B$ = the event of getting an odd number: tap on the number line every outcome in $B$.
items.construction: Points mode, range [-6,6]. Tap 1, 3 and 5. That is 3 targets, all whole numbers inside the range, so it is valid.
items.predicate_meaning: Right sizes, wrong signs — a value marked as its negative, as when (x − a) = 0 is read as x = −a
items.hint: Check each marked outcome against the condition of the event.
items.why: It can fire, for example on -1, -3 and -5. But the sample space is positive, and a sign flip is not the likely error here. The hint does not point at the sign, so it does not help the student find the step they got wrong.

items.stem: A die is thrown, so the sample space is $S=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$. Write the event $C$ = the event of getting a prime even number: tap on the number line every outcome in $C$.
items.construction: Points mode, range [-6,6]. Primes in S are 2,3,5; evens are 2,4,6; both: only 2. Tap 2 only (targets=[2]); within range, a whole number, 1 target.
items.predicate_meaning: Right sizes, wrong signs — a value marked as its negative, as when (x − a) = 0 is read as x = −a
items.hint: Check each marked outcome against both conditions.
items.why: It can fire, e.g. if the student taps -2 instead of 2. But the hint is generic and does not point to the sign slip. The sign-flip idea (x−a=0 read as x=−a) has nothing to do with a die outcome question, so the hint does not help the student find the step they got wrong. Rejected.

items.stem: A classroom contains 40 students. 18 of them read Al-Akhbar newspaper, 15 read Al-Ahram newspaper and 8 read both newspapers. A student is selected randomly. Fill in the number of students in each region of the Venn diagram, then find the probability that the student reads Al-Akhbar newspaper only.
items.construction: Enter a=10 (Al-Akhbar only), b=7 (Al-Ahram only), ab=8 (both), n=15 (neither). Sum = 40 = total. Clues a=10+8=18 and b=7+8=15 are consistent. All values are whole numbers in 0–999. The probability part (10/40 = 1/4) is outside the widget, but the counts are fully buildable.
items.predicate_meaning: A region's raw set size was entered instead of the count exclusive to it — the overlap counted in twice
items.misconception_label: Counts the whole set A when asked for A only
items.misconception_description: The student takes the 'only' event A - B to be the whole set A, so they use all of A's students and never remove the overlap A ∩ B.
items.why: The predicate can fire here, because clues are present. It fires when a region holds the raw set size (a=18 or b=15) instead of the exclusive count. But the misconception is 'only means whole set A': the student takes A-only to be all of A. A student who enters 18 in the A-only region while also entering 8 in the overlap does double-count the overlap, so some firings would fit. The predicate can't tell this error from a student who simply doesn't subtract, for example one who enters 18 and 15 as raw sizes in both circles. It would also fire for B's raw size, which the misconception (about A only) doesn't cover. The match is partial, and the question asks for counts in every region, not for A only alone. When in doubt, false.
